decisions.reason: The same-message MODIFY already records full ESP32-S3 pin coverage, through-hole breakout format, and reusable-platform purpose. The proposed 1.27 mm pitch remains a question rather than a confirmed change.
The source concerns routing space and ESP32 breakout access on the main board, not the power board's mechanical form factor.
Reusing the main board as an ESP32-S3 base platform does not change the existing three-board architecture or the defined roles of those boards.
The routing-space and breakout-access decision does not alter the requirement to place the ESP32 antenna at the PCB edge.
The source establishes general routing-space and pin-breakout constraints but does not change connector placement, alignment, or cable-routing requirements.
The main-board routing-space discussion does not modify the power board's four-layer stack or grounding strategy.
Retaining access to every ESP32-S3 pin and sufficient PCB routing space does not change standalone USB power behavior or its powered loads.
The source does not alter the panel reset connector, its electrical action, or its physical implementation.
The main-board routing and breakout requirements do not change the switched 5V rail's control, loads, or operating policy.
The source does not change I2C cable length, speed, pull-ups, or optional series-resistor conditioning.
The source decision does not affect DCDC1 voltage, current capacity, or Schottky-drop compensation.
Requiring physical access to every module pin does not itself reassign any GPIO or change the confirmed GPIO pool.
